explanation: Italy has no taboo against the left hand; in fact, Continental European table manners keep the fork in the left hand (knife in the right) throughout the entire meal, unlike the American style of switching hands. The old Western stigma against left-handedness itself (once called 'the devil's hand') was about forcing children to write right-handed, not about food hygiene like the toilet-related taboo found in parts of South Asia or the Middle East.
local_tip: Eat Continental-style with the fork in your left hand and knife in your right — switching hands repeatedly looks more unusual than left-hand use itself.

also_check.note: Eating with the left hand is widely seen as rude; the left hand is reserved for bathroom hygiene.
The left hand is considered unclean; eat with the right hand, especially from shared dishes.
No stigma against left-handed eating; left-handedness is fully accepted at the table.
